frequency_question: How often does a central bank implement an incremental reserve ratio requirement within a roughly 4-month operational window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal secondary reserve ratio hikes or incremental CRR deployments by systemically important emerging market central banks during periods of acute capital inflows or liquidity overhang; excludes standard standing facility rate adjustments.
window: Any designated 4-month operational window within the historical observation period.

cases.name: Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement adjustment
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit adjustment
RBI prior liquidity absorption scheme historical analogue

provenance_note: claims 20 cases from only 5 named (4.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 5 named benchmark episodes; believed roughly 20 comparable major tightening/liquidity-absorption policy windows globally in similar contexts.
known_gaps: Varies by jurisdiction depending on structural liquidity deficit or surplus frameworks.
skeleton: Major emerging market central bank policy cycles over the past two decades where liquidity management tools of this specific category were considered, multiplied by the frequency of targeted incremental reserve requirement utilization.
multiplier: 5 historical comparable episodes identified across major emerging market jurisdictions over a 20-year sample space yielding a low base rate of episodic deployment.
validity_reason: Central bank operational toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year secular cycles.
